screenSummary.playArea: An outdoor scene with a pool set into the ground. Sky and air are above the ground line; earth and the pool are below it. Barometers can be placed anywhere to read the pressure there.
screenSummary.controlArea: Controls for the pool scene, the atmosphere, the units of every readout, the fluid in the pool, the strength of gravity, and a Reset All button.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Choose a pool, then drag a barometer into the water and move it up and down to see how pressure changes with depth.

underPressure.currentDetails: Showing the {{scene}}. {{placed}} of {{total}} barometers are placed. The atmosphere is {{atmosphere}}.

screenSummary.playArea: A pipe running left to right below the ground, carrying fluid from a source off the left of the screen. Handles on the pipe wall change its shape; dots carried along in the fluid show how fast it is moving.
screenSummary.controlArea: Controls for the flow rate, wall friction, the flux meter, the marker dots, the ruler, the units of every readout, the fluid in the pipe, playback speed, and a Reset All button.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Drag a pipe handle to narrow the pipe, then watch the dots and the barometer to see what happens to the speed and the pressure.

flow.currentDetails: The fluid is flowing at {{flowRate}}. {{placed}} of {{total}} sensors are placed.

screenSummary.playArea: A water tower standing on the ground with a faucet above it and a hole near its base. Water leaving the hole falls as a stream that can be measured.
screenSummary.controlArea: Controls for the faucet, the sluice gate, the hose, the ruler, the measuring tape, the units of every readout, the fluid in the tank, playback speed, and a Reset All button.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Open the hole at the base of the tank, then raise and lower the tank to see how the height of the water changes the speed of the stream.

waterTower.currentDetails: The tank is {{fill}} percent full and the hole at its base is {{hole}}.

preferences.linkUnitsDescription: When on, choosing a unit system on one screen sets it on all three.
